description.en: An OWL 2 ontology modelling the STIX 2.1 specification. Provides a class hierarchy for all STIX Domain Objects (SDOs), Cyber Observable Objects (SCOs), Relationship Objects (SROs), Meta Objects, and structured sub-types, together with datatype and object properties covering all standard STIX properties.

definition.value: Defines a data handling marking used to restrict or label how STIX data can be shared or handled, such as TLP markings. Referenced by object_marking_refs or granular_markings.
A mistake in software that can be directly used by a threat actor to gain access to a system or network. Typically identified by a CVE number via an external reference.
Abstract class for STIX Cyber Observable Objects (SCOs), which represent technical observations such as IP addresses, files, network traffic, and processes.

Represents a sequence of bytes, such as the content of a file, a raw stream of network traffic, or a data blob captured from memory. The content may be embedded directly via payload_bin or referenced via url.
Provides translations of string properties of another STIX object into different languages. Allows internationalisation without modifying the original object.
A type of TTP that represents malicious code. Captures both malware families (when is_family is true) and specific instances or samples.
A property-level data handling marking that applies a marking definition to specific named fields of a STIX object, enabling fine-grained access control.
Represents an arbitrary network traffic flow between source and destination endpoints. Supports extensions for HTTP, ICMP, socket, and TCP specifics.
Represents a single email address, optionally associating it with a display name and a user account.
Abstract class for STIX Relationship Objects (SROs), which link Core Objects to express directed relationships and sightings between them.
Represents a file with its metadata and optional content reference. Supports extensions for archive files, NTFS streams, PE binaries, PDF documents, and raster images.
A structured reference to non-STIX information, such as a CVE entry, MITRE ATT&CK technique, or external URL. Used to link STIX content to authoritative external sources.
An assessment of the correctness of information in one or more STIX objects. Allows analysts to express agreement or disagreement with existing intelligence.
The set of X.509 version 3 extension fields present in a digital certificate, such as key usage, subject alternative names, and CRL distribution points.
Represents a Uniform Resource Locator conforming to RFC 3986.
A single section entry within a Windows PE (Portable Executable) binary, described by its name, size, and optional entropy value.
Contains a pattern that can be used to detect suspicious or malicious cyber activity. Patterns are expressed using the STIX Patterning Language or another supported pattern language.
A collection of threat intelligence focused on one or more topics, such as a description of a threat actor, malware, or attack technique. Used to package related STIX content.
Represents a named mutual-exclusion object, commonly created or checked by malware to prevent multiple concurrent instances from running.
Represents an email message, including its headers, body, and any MIME parts.
Abstract class for STIX Core Objects, comprising SDOs, SCOs, and SROs. Core objects carry a type-qualified identifier and created/modified timestamps, and may be referenced by other objects.
Represents one or more IPv6 addresses expressed using CIDR notation.
Explicitly asserts that a set of STIX objects share a common context without implying the existence of a threat report. Useful for linking related objects without a formal report.
An NTFS Alternate Data Stream (ADS) attached to a file, identified by name with optional hashes and size.
Records that a STIX object such as an indicator, malware, tool, or threat actor was seen. Wraps observation metadata around a reference to the sighted object.
A single value entry within a Windows Registry key, comprising a name, a data string, and a registry data type.
The top-level abstract class for all STIX objects, encompassing STIX Core Objects (SDOs, SCOs, SROs), Meta Objects, and Bundles.
Represents a user account on a system or service, including local OS accounts, cloud accounts, and social media accounts. Supports a unix-account extension for POSIX attributes.
Represents a Windows Registry key with its full path, value entries, modification timestamp, and creator.
A grouped set of adversarial behaviours and resources with common properties, believed to be orchestrated by a single organisation. Often represents a named APT group.
Represents a software product, including commercial applications, operating systems, libraries, and utilities.
A directed link between two STIX Core Objects. The semantics of the link are defined by the relationship_type property.
Represents a phase within a named kill chain framework, such as the MITRE ATT&CK or Lockheed Martin Cyber Kill Chain, used to categorise the stage of an attack.
Represents an Autonomous System (AS), a collection of IP routing prefixes under the control of a single administrative entity, identified by its AS number.
Conveys information observed on systems and networks, wrapping one or more SCO references together with observation metadata such as first and last observed timestamps.
Actual individuals, groups, or organisations believed to be operating with malicious intent. Unlike Identity, a ThreatActor carries adversarial connotations.
Represents one or more IPv4 addresses expressed using CIDR notation.
Conveys informational text to provide further context and/or to assess the accuracy of existing STIX information. Similar to a comment or annotation on other STIX objects.
Represents a network domain name. Can reference the IP addresses it resolves to.
Defines a schema extension to STIX 2.1. Allows producers to add new properties or new object types in a structured, interoperable way.
A single cryptographic hash entry associating a hashing algorithm with its hex-encoded digest value. Used to represent entries in the STIX hashes dictionary.
A single MIME part within a multipart email message, including its body content, content type, and content disposition.
A type of Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTP) that describes ways that adversaries attempt to compromise targets. Often maps to MITRE ATT&CK techniques.

Abstract class for structured sub-types defined by the STIX 2.1 specification that are embedded as property values within STIX objects. Instances are not STIX objects: they carry no identifier, type, spec_version, created, or modified properties and cannot be referenced by identifier from other objects. Subclasses include ExternalReference, GranularMarking, KillChainPhase, HashEntry, EmailMimePart, AlternateDataStream, WindowsPeSection, WindowsRegistryValue, and X509V3Extensions.
Abstract class for STIX Domain Objects (SDOs), which represent modelled cyber threat intelligence concepts such as malware, campaigns, threat actors, and vulnerabilities.
Represents a file system directory, conveying its path and timestamps. May reference the files and sub-directories it contains.
Legitimate software that can be used by threat actors to perform attacks. Distinguishable from malware by being designed for benign purposes but repurposed maliciously.
Represents a single MAC address expressed in lowercase IEEE 802 colon-hexadecimal notation.
Actual individuals, organisations, or groups, as well as classes of individuals, organisations, systems, or groups. Used to represent victims, producers, or any other real-world actor.
A grouping of adversary behaviours and resources with a common objective pursued over a period of time. Campaigns may be attributed to intrusion sets or threat actors.
Captures the results of a malware analysis process, whether static or dynamic. Represents the output of a specific analysis run on a specific sample.
Represents a running or terminated process on a host. Supports extensions for Windows-specific process and service attributes.
A collection of arbitrary STIX objects used as a transport container. Bundles are not Core Objects, carry no modified timestamp, and cannot be referenced by identifier.
A recommendation for a specific measure to be taken in response to an attack. May describe automated responses, playbook steps, or manual mitigations.
Represents a geographic location. May be as specific as a latitude/longitude coordinate or as broad as a continent. At least one of region, country, or latitude/longitude must be provided.
Represents an X.509 digital certificate, capturing its subject, issuer, validity window, public key details, and optional v3 extensions.
Abstract class for STIX Meta Objects, which provide supporting infrastructure for the STIX ecosystem, including data markings, language translations, and extension definitions.
Represents systems, software services, or any group of resources used to conduct cyber operations. Infrastructure is used by threat actors and intrusion sets both offensively and defensively.
If true, this sighting aggregates multiple observations rather than recording a single specific event.
Reference to the network-traffic SCO that encapsulates (wraps) this flow.
Full Windows Registry key path, e.g. 'HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\...'.
Latitude in decimal degrees, range -90 to 90. Required when longitude is present.
The STIX object type string, e.g. 'attack-pattern'. Semantically redundant with rdf:type but preserved for JSON round-tripping.
Current status of this Windows service (windows-service-status-enum): SERVICE_RUNNING, SERVICE_STOPPED, SERVICE_PAUSED, etc.
True if this socket is in blocking mode.
Current working directory of the process.
Street address.
Name of the software vendor.
Pattern language used by this indicator (pattern-type-ov): stix, pcre, sigma, snort, suricata, yara.
References to Identity SDOs representing where or by whom the sighting was recorded.
Last modification timestamp of this registry key.
RSA modulus of the subject's public key as a hex string.
True if this is a service or system account rather than a user account.
Last-modified timestamp of a file system object.
Radius of accuracy in metres around the latitude/longitude point.
Windows registry value entries under this key. Each entry is a stones:WindowsRegistryValue individual.
Description strings for a Windows service. Multiple values as multiple triples.
References to network-traffic SCOs representing connections this process has opened.
Primary motivation driving this intrusion set or threat actor (attack-motivation-ov).
Windows service type (windows-service-type-enum): SERVICE_KERNEL_DRIVER, SERVICE_FILE_SYSTEM_DRIVER, SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS, SERVICE_WIN32_SHARE_PROCESS.
References to file or artifact SCOs that are samples of this malware.
References to file SCOs for DLLs loaded by this Windows service.
Free-form string terms applying to this object. Multiple labels are expressed as multiple triples.
Windows integrity level of this process (windows-integrity-level-enum): low, medium, high, system.
PE binary subtype (windows-pebinary-type-ov): exe, dll, or sys.
Start of the certificate validity period.
True if Data Execution Prevention (DEP) is enabled for this process.
ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, e.g. 'US', 'GB'.
Names of analysis modules or plugins used. Multiple values as multiple triples.
Version of the analysis definitions or signatures.
ISO/IEC 19770-2 SWID tag identifier.
References to STIX objects included in or annotated by this grouping, report, note, opinion, or observed-data. For observed-data the referenced objects MUST be SCOs.
Personal motivations of this threat actor, distinct from organisational motivations (attack-motivation-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Human-readable name. Used across SDOs, SCOs, and sub-objects.
Colour depth of the image in bits per pixel.
References to software SCOs describing the operating systems this malware targets or runs on.
STIX specification version. MUST be '2.1'.
References to network-traffic SCOs encapsulated within this flow, e.g. inner tunnelled protocols.
Names of the authors of a note or opinion. Multiple values are expressed as multiple triples.
Number of packets sent from destination to source.
X.509 v3 name constraints extension value.
Reference to the artifact SCO containing the destination-to-source payload bytes.
Title text of the main window of this Windows process.
Windows service name as used in the Service Control Manager.
Hashes of the PE file header, expressed as HashEntry individuals.
The STIX Core Object at the target (end) of this relationship.
BCP 47 language tag for the human-readable content of this object, e.g. 'en', 'fr'. Also used in GranularMarking.
Primary string value of an observable: the domain name, email address, IP address, MAC address, or URL.
X.509 v3 certificate policies extension.
Detection pattern expression, e.g. a STIX patterning language expression.
X.509 v3 subject alternative name extension.
Timestamp recorded in the PE header.
Primary goal or objective of the campaign.
Skill and knowledge level of this threat actor (threat-actor-sophistication-ov): none, minimal, intermediate, advanced, expert, innovator, strategic.
Level of agreement expressed by this opinion (opinion-enum): strongly-disagree, disagree, neutral, agree, strongly-agree.
Earliest timestamp at which this observation occurred.
Timestamp when the account credentials were last changed.
True if this certificate is self-signed.
Home directory path for this UNIX account.
Reference to the STIX object whose string properties are being translated by this language-content object.
Scheduling priority string for this Windows process, e.g. 'HIGH_PRIORITY_CLASS'.
Value of the Content-Type header (email-message, email MIME part).
X.509 v3 issuer alternative name extension.
Functional categories of this tool (tool-type-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Categories of intelligence covered by this report (report-type-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
ICMP code field as a hex value.
References to email-addr SCOs in the Bcc: header.
JSON property path selectors identifying the properties this marking applies to, e.g. 'name', 'description'. Multiple values as multiple triples.
True if this network traffic flow was still active when it was observed.
Classification name from the analysis product.
Timestamp when this object was created.
File offset of the COFF symbol table as hex.
Type of entity represented by this identity (identity-class-ov): individual, group, system, organization, class, unknown.
Timestamp when this relationship began.
Serial number assigned to this certificate by the issuer.
Reference to the artifact SCO containing the HTTP message body.
References to email-addr SCOs in the To: header.
Name of the analysis tool used, e.g. 'Cuckoo', 'VirusTotal'.
Producer's confidence in the accuracy of this data, from 0 (no confidence) to 100 (fully confident).
Name of the information source, e.g. 'mitre-attack', 'cve', 'capec'.
Reference to the MarkingDefinition applied by this granular marking entry.
Hex-encoded hash digest value.
Reference to an artifact or file SCO containing the raw bytes of this MIME part.
Service start type (windows-service-start-type-enum): SERVICE_AUTO_START, SERVICE_BOOT_START, SERVICE_DEMAND_START, SERVICE_DISABLED, SERVICE_SYSTEM_ALERT.
Data stored in this Windows registry value.
X.509 v3 basic constraints extension value.
Date and time the email was sent as recorded in the Date header.
Clear-text credential associated with this account. Handle with care.
BCP 47 language tags for languages supported by this software. Multiple values as multiple triples.
X.509 v3 key usage extension value.
Size of the optional PE header in bytes.
References to child process SCOs spawned by this process.
Type of user account (account-type-ov): facebook, ldap, nis, openid, radius, skype, tacacs, twitter, unix, windows-domain, windows-local.
PE section entries for this binary. Each entry is a stones:WindowsPeSection individual.
Primary numeric UNIX group ID (GID).
Image width in pixels.
Reference to the source address SCO for this network traffic flow (ipv4-addr, ipv6-addr, mac-addr, or domain-name).
Full command line string used to launch this process.
Number of times the sighted object was observed. MUST be >= 0.
Timestamp of the first login for this account.
Content-Disposition header value for an email MIME part.
If true, this process is hidden from normal process enumeration.
Characteristics flags from the PE COFF header as hex.
X.509 v3 inhibit any policy extension.
Timestamp when this network traffic flow started.
Brief summary of the note.
True if this account has elevated privileges.
End of the private key usage period.
The STIX identifier string in the format <type>--<UUIDv4>. The IRI of the individual is the canonical identity; this property retains the string for JSON round-tripping and SPARQL querying.
Decryption key for this artifact when it is encrypted.
Programming languages used to implement this malware (implementation-language-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Timestamp from which this indicator is considered valid.
Comment field embedded in an archive file.
URL pointing to, or the raw content of, the JSON Schema defining this extension.
Kill chain phase(s) associated with this attack-pattern, indicator, infrastructure, malware, or tool.
X.509 v3 CRL distribution points extension.
X.509 v3 extended key usage extension value.
Algorithm of the subject's public key, e.g. 'rsaEncryption'.
Creation timestamp of a file system object.
TCP flags set on packets from the source endpoint as hex, e.g. '0x02' for SYN.
Version of the analysis tool configuration.
Type of this socket (network-socket-type-enum): SOCK_STREAM, SOCK_DGRAM, SOCK_RAW, SOCK_RDM, SOCK_SEQPACKET.
Timestamp when this object was last observed or seen. MUST be >= firstSeen.
Number of subkeys under this registry key.
Categories of this threat actor (threat-actor-type-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Character encoding used for the path property when the path contains non-ASCII characters.
True if the PDF is linearized (optimised for fast web viewing).
UN M.49 macro-geographical region (region-ov).
Industry sectors this identity operates in (industry-sector-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Property-level data-handling markings targeting specific fields of this object.
Length of the HTTP message body in bytes.
Numeric UNIX user ID (UID).
Reference to the directory SCO that contains this file.
Magic bytes (file signature) as a hex string.
Image height in pixels.
Human-readable display name (email-addr, user-account, windows-service-ext).
For domain-name: references to ipv4-addr, ipv6-addr, or domain-name SCOs this domain resolves to. For ipv4-addr or ipv6-addr: references to mac-addr SCOs.
Reference to the email-addr SCO in the Sender: header.
Timestamp when analysis concluded.
Reference to the user-account SCO of the user who created this process or registry key.
Names of new top-level properties introduced by a toplevel-property-extension. Multiple values as multiple triples.
Functional capabilities exhibited by this malware (malware-capabilities-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Reference to the artifact SCO containing the source-to-destination payload bytes.
Reference to the parent process SCO of this process.
Start of the private key usage period.
True if this email uses multipart MIME (bodyMultipart is populated); false if body contains the single plain-text body.
Timestamp when analysis began.
Version of the analysis engine.
Reference to the file SCO of the executable image that was launched to create this process.
Import hash (imphash) of the PE binary.
Raw classification string from an antivirus engine, e.g. 'Trojan.GenericKD'.
Type of marking definition: 'tlp' or 'statement'.
Subject line of an email message, or Distinguished Name of the certificate subject.
IANA MIME type of the content (artifact, file).
Timestamp when the sample was submitted for analysis.
Version string. Used for analysis tool version (malware-analysis), schema version (extension-definition), software version, X.509 version, and PDF format version.
References to non-STIX information sources such as CVEs, ATT&CK techniques, or URLs.
Categories of this indicator (indicator-type-ov): anomalous-activity, anonymization, benign, compromised, malicious-activity, attribution, unknown.
ICMP type field as a hex value.
End of the certificate validity period.
Reference to the user-account SCO that owns this email address.
Version string of the tool.
Reference to the software SCO describing the virtual machine used for analysis.
How this extension definition is used (extension-types-enum): new-sdo, new-sco, new-sro, property-extension, toplevel-property-extension. Multiple values as multiple triples.
Contact details such as email address or phone number.
Analysis verdict for this malware analysis (malware-result-ov): malicious, suspicious, benign, unknown.
X.509 v3 authority key identifier.
References to software SCOs installed in the analysis environment.
Number of times the observation occurred. MUST be >= 1.
Timestamp when this account was created.
True if this account is currently disabled.
True if this account can escalate its own privileges.
Timestamp of the most recent login for this account.
Total bytes sent from source to destination.
Source port number (0–65535).
Shared context that motivates this grouping (grouping-context-ov).
Distinguished Name of the certificate issuer.
Reference to the Identity SDO that created this STIX object.
Additional motivations beyond the primary motivation (attack-motivation-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
NTFS Alternate Data Streams present on this file. Each entry is a stones:AlternateDataStream individual.
Names of UNIX groups this account belongs to. Multiple values as multiple triples.
X.509 v3 subject key identifier.
True if this socket is in a listening state.
Artifact byte content encoded as base64. Mutually exclusive with url.
If true, this object has been revoked and should no longer be considered accurate.
Identifier of the user account, such as a login name or UID.
Number of sections in the PE binary.
Semantic type of this relationship, e.g. 'uses', 'targets', 'indicates'.
Received: header values in the order received. Multiple values as multiple triples.
Encryption algorithm applied to this artifact (encryption-algorithm-enum). Required when decryptionKey is present.
Platform-specific socket file descriptor number.
Algorithm used to sign this certificate, e.g. 'sha256WithRSAEncryption'.
STIX objects (SDOs, SCOs, SROs, meta-objects) carried in this bundle.
Timestamp when this object was last modified. MUST be >= created.
Version of the pattern language, e.g. the STIX patterning language version.
Absolute file system path (directory, file).
Reference to the artifact SCO containing the full raw email bytes.
Timestamp when this relationship ended. MUST be >= startTime.
Reference to the software SCO describing the operating system used for analysis.
Last-accessed timestamp of a file system object.
Explanation of why this opinion was formed.
State, province, or region within a country.
Date and time this report was published.
Number of entries in the COFF symbol table.
Size in bytes (file, windows-pe-section, alternate-data-stream).
References to SCOs generated or observed as a result of this analysis.
Calculated entropy of this PE section.
Value of the Message-ID header.
Data type of this Windows registry value (windows-registry-datatype-enum): REG_NONE, REG_SZ, REG_EXPAND_SZ, REG_BINARY, REG_DWORD, etc.
RSA public exponent of the subject's public key.
City name.
X.509 v3 extension fields for this certificate.
Destination port number (0–65535).
Processor architectures this malware can execute on (processor-architecture-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
X.509 v3 authority information access extension.
URL to a referenced resource (external-reference) or the location of artifact content.
First PDF file identifier string from the PDF trailer.
Second PDF file identifier string from the PDF trailer.
True if this represents a malware family; false for a specific instance or sample.
Alternative names for this object. Multiple aliases are expressed as multiple triples.
MIME parts of a multipart email message. Each part is a stones:EmailMimePart individual.
X.509 v3 policy constraints extension value.
Functional categories of this infrastructure (infrastructure-type-ov).
Identifier in the external system, e.g. 'T1059', 'CVE-2021-44228'.
Process ID (PID).
Total bytes sent from destination to source.
Machine type from the COFF header as a hex value.
Longitude in decimal degrees, range -180 to 180. Required when latitude is present.
The hashing algorithm used for this hash entry (hashing-algorithm-ov).
X.509 v3 subject directory attributes extension.
Timestamp when the process was created.
The modified timestamp of the STIX object being translated. Used to pin a translation to a specific version.
NVD CPE 2.3 URI binding identifier for this software.
HTTP version string, e.g. 'HTTP/1.1'.
Autonomous System number (ASN).
Plain-text body of an email message or a MIME part.
Login shell path for this UNIX account, e.g. '/bin/bash'.
Latest timestamp at which this observation occurred. MUST be >= firstObserved.
Functional categories of this malware (malware-type-ov). Multiple values as multiple triples.
Reference to the destination address SCO for this network traffic flow.
Human-readable description providing additional detail.
Windows Security Identifier (SID) of the file owner (ntfs-ext) or process owner (windows-process-ext).
High-level goals of this intrusion set or threat actor, e.g. 'financial gain'. Multiple values are expressed as multiple triples.
Number of packets sent from source to destination.
Resource level available to this intrusion set or threat actor (attack-resource-level-ov): individual, club, contest, team, organization, government.
Address family of this socket (network-socket-address-family-enum): AF_UNSPEC, AF_INET, AF_INET6, AF_IPX, AF_APPLETALK, AF_NETBIOS, AF_IRDA, AF_BTH.
Timestamp when this network traffic flow ended.
X.509 v3 policy mappings extension.
If true, the observable has been defanged, e.g. '198[.]51[.]100[.]0' in place of '198.51.100.0'.
Character encoding of the file name when non-ASCII characters are present.
Windows handle value for this socket.
HTTP method, e.g. 'GET', 'POST'.
TLP level for a TLP marking definition: 'white', 'green', 'amber', or 'red'.
Timestamp after which this indicator is no longer valid.
True if Address Space Layout Randomisation (ASLR) is enabled for this process.
Load ordering group for this Windows service.
Ordered list of protocols from lowest to highest layer, e.g. 'ipv4', 'tcp', 'http'. Multiple values as multiple triples.
Name of the kill chain framework, e.g. 'mitre-attack', 'lockheed-martin-cyber-kill-chain'.
TCP flags set on packets from the destination endpoint as hex.
Timestamp when this account expires.
References to file or directory SCOs contained within this directory or archive.
Regional Internet Registry that assigned this ASN, e.g. 'ARIN', 'RIPE'.
Reference to the artifact SCO that holds the content of this file.
Reference to the email-addr SCO in the From: header.
Roles this threat actor plays in an attack (threat-actor-role-ov): agent, director, independent, infrastructure-architect, infrastructure-operator, malware-author, sponsor.
Reference to the STIX Core Object that was sighted. Typically an indicator, malware, campaign, threat-actor, intrusion-set, tool, attack-pattern, or infrastructure.
Human-readable statement for a statement marking definition, e.g. a copyright notice.
HTTP request URI path, e.g. '/index.html?q=1'.
References to autonomous-system SCOs that own this IP address.
References to email-addr SCOs in the Cc: header.
Free-form roles this identity plays, e.g. 'analyst'. For threat-actor roles see the object property stones:threatActorRoles.
Full body text of the note.
Timestamp when this object was first observed or seen.
References to MarkingDefinition objects that apply data-handling markings to this entire object.
References to ObservedData SDOs that provide evidence supporting this sighting.
Cryptographic hashes of an artifact, file, certificate, or other content, expressed as a set of HashEntry individuals.
Postal or ZIP code.
Phase within the kill chain, e.g. 'execution', 'persistence', 'lateral-movement'.
Login name if different from userId.
The STIX Core Object at the source (start) of this relationship.
